### From the Śrīmad Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddhakāṇḍa

७३०

Bears, lions, wild boars, buffaloes, elephants, and deer were terrified by that sound and fled in all ten directions <note>the four cardinal points, four intermediate points, zenith, and nadir</note>. There stood a peak of Mount Trikūṭa, high and touching the sky, covered all over with flowers and shining like precious gold <note>original: "mahārajata-sannibham"; while "rajata" usually means silver, in this context it refers to the brilliance of gold or refined metal</note>. १८

It was a hundred <term>yojanas</term> <gloss>a measure of distance, roughly eight to nine miles</gloss> wide, pure and beautiful to behold. Smooth, majestic, and so vast that even birds could barely reach it. १९

It was difficult to ascend even in thought, much less by physical action. On that peak sat the city of Laṅkā, protected by Rāvaṇa. २०

The city was a hundred <term>yojanas</term> wide and thirty <term>yojanas</term> long. It was adorned with high gates that resembled white clouds. २१

Laṅkā was fortified with walls of gold and silver and beautifully decorated with palaces and <term>vimānas</term> <gloss>aerial chariots or celestial mansions</gloss>. २२

Like clouds at the end of the summer heat, there stood a palace supported by a thousand pillars. २३

It rose up like a peak of Mount Kailāsa, seemingly scraping the sky. This <term>caitya</term> <gloss>a sacred building or palatial shrine</gloss> of the Lord of Demons was the crowning jewel of the city. २४

It was guarded constantly by a full hundred demons. Rāma, the fortunate elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, looked upon Rāvaṇa's city together with the monkeys. The city was delightful, filled with forests and graced by hills of various colorful minerals. २५, २६

It was adorned with gardens, filled with the songs of various birds, and inhabited by diverse groups of beings. २७

Covered in many types of flowers and populated by various demons, the city drew its wealth from the sea. Seeing that city crowded with great mansions, resembling the city of the gods, the powerful elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa was filled with wonder. २८

Rāma, accompanied by his great army, gazed upon that city filled with gems and complex structures, adorned with rows of palaces and secured by massive mechanical gates. २९

<note>Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter of the Yuddhakāṇḍa in the glorious Rāmāyaṇa of Vālmīki, the first epic poem, consisting of twenty-four thousand verses, entitled "The Sight of Laṅkā."</note>

---

### Chapter 40
**The Duel between Rāvaṇa and Sugrīva**

Then Rāma, accompanied by Sugrīva and the leaders of the monkey host, ascended the summit of Mount Suvela, which was two <term>yojanas</term> in circumference. १

Standing there for a moment and looking out in all ten directions, he saw Laṅkā. It was well-situated on the beautiful peak of Mount Trikūṭa, built by the divine architect Viśvakarman and adorned with lovely forests. २

On the top of a gate-tower, he saw the formidable King of Demons. ३

He was flanked by white <term>cāmaras</term> <gloss>whisks made of yak-tail hair, symbols of royalty</gloss> and shielded by the umbrella of victory. He was anointed with red sandalwood paste and decorated with gemstone ornaments. ४

He appeared like a dark rain-cloud, dressed in garments embroidered with gold. His chest bore the prominent scars made by the tusks of the celestial elephant Airāvata. ५

Wrapped in a red cloth as bright as the blood of a rabbit, he looked like a mass of clouds in the sky illuminated by the glow of twilight. ६

While the monkey chiefs and Rāma were watching, Sugrīva suddenly sprang up at the sight of the King of Demons. ७

<note>1. This half-verse is missing in some manuscript editions.</note>

<summary>Rāma and the monkey army arrive at Mount Suvela and gaze upon the magnificent, heavily fortified city of Laṅkā. Upon spotting Rāvaṇa standing atop his palace gates, the monkey king Sugrīva is overcome with impulse and leaps into action.</summary>
